d: RodConstraint keeps two attachments separated by a defined length, with optional limits on rotational tilt.
h:
For an overview on creating, visualizing, and simulating mechanical constraints, including RodConstraint, see Mechanical constraints. Also see Roblox units to understand how Roblox units compare to metric units.

A RodConstraint keeps two attachments separated by its defined Length. By default, both attachments can rotate freely, although you can enable limits to restrict rotational tilt.

Limits

You can limit rotation of the attachments within a cone, independently of each other, by enabling the LimitsEnabled property and setting LimitAngle0 and LimitAngle1 respectively.

kid.simple: A RodConstraint keeps two attachments exactly the same distance apart, like a stiff stick between them. Unlike a rope, a rod pushes as well as pulls, so the parts can never get closer or farther. Both ends can swivel freely, but you can limit how far each end can tilt. Rods are great for pendulums, wrecking balls, and linkages in machines.
kid.analogy: It is like a stick with a loose joint at each end, such as the arm of a playground swing made of metal bars instead of chains.
keyPoints: A rod keeps its two attachments separated by exactly its `Length` in studs.
Unlike a RopeConstraint, the attachments cannot move closer together either.
Both attachments can rotate freely by default.
Turn on `LimitsEnabled` and set `LimitAngle0` and `LimitAngle1` to limit how far each end can tilt, each within its own cone.
`CurrentDistance` tells you how far apart the attachments are right now.

terms.attachment: A Roblox object you put inside a part to mark one exact point on it. Its Position is measured from the part's center, so an attachment at (0, 3, 0) sits 3 studs above the center of its part.
terms.Length: The exact distance the rod keeps. With Length 8, the attachments stay 8 studs apart, never 7 or 9.
terms.rod vs rope: A rope only stops things getting too far apart. A rod also stops them getting too close.
terms.LimitAngle0 / LimitAngle1: How far, in degrees, the rod may tilt at the Attachment0 end and at the Attachment1 end. Each end gets its own limit.
terms.cone: The shape made by all allowed tilt directions. A 30 degree limit makes a narrow cone; 90 makes a wide one.
terms.pendulum: A weight that swings back and forth on a rod or string, like in a grandfather clock.

example.title: A swinging pendulum
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local pivot = Instance.new("Part")
pivot.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
pivot.Position = Vector3.new(20, 20, 0)
pivot.Anchored = true
pivot.Parent = Workspace

local bob = Instance.new("Part")
bob.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
bob.Size = Vector3.new(2, 2, 2)
bob.Material = Enum.Material.Metal
bob.Position = Vector3.new(28, 20, 0)  -- 8 studs to the side, level with the pivot
bob.Parent = Workspace

local pivotAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
pivotAtt.Parent = pivot

local bobAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
bobAtt.Parent = bob

local rod = Instance.new("RodConstraint")
rod.Attachment0 = pivotAtt
rod.Attachment1 = bobAtt
rod.Length = 8
rod.Visible = true
rod.Parent = pivot
explain: The pivot is anchored. The ball starts 8 studs to the side at the same height, so the rod is level.
Gravity pulls the ball down, but the rod keeps it exactly 8 studs from the pivot, so it swings in an arc and back up the other side.
For small swings, a pendulum this long takes roughly 2 x 3.14 x the square root of (8 / 196.2), about 1.3 seconds, to swing there and back.
If you make `Length` 4 times bigger (32), the swing takes about twice as long. Pendulum timing grows with the square root of the length.
If this were a rope instead, the ball could bounce up toward the pivot. The rod stops that.

watchOut: If you set `Length` very different from the starting distance, the parts snap together or apart when the game starts. Place them at about the right distance first.
A rod cannot be powered. For a motor-driven swing, use a HingeConstraint.
